title: Spin Talent Radar: What Separates a Prospect from a Starter for Punjab Kings?
dek: What separates a spin prospect from a starter? Comparing newer IPL spinners with established ones in the middle overs shows where the gap really lies.
excerpt: Since 2024, newer IPL spinners have conceded more per over in the middle overs than established ones. The gap between prospect and starter is smaller, or larger, than reputations suggest, and the data shows which.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Prospect or Starter?
body: Spin is the skill where youth is most often doubted: captains trust experienced spinners to bowl in the middle overs. The question is whether the data supports that caution.
CricField compared spinners who debuted in 2023 or later with those who debuted by 2020, in overs seven to fifteen since 2024 (min. one hundred and twenty balls).

sections.heading: The Gap
body: Newer spinners conceded {{ev:sr-pe}} an over and took a wicket every {{ev:sr-pw}} balls. Established spinners conceded {{ev:sr-ee}} and took a wicket every {{ev:sr-ew}} balls.
The chart lists the most economical of the {{ev:sr-pn}} newer spinners who qualified.

sections.heading: Limits
body: Spinners are identified from player-bio bowling styles, which cover bowlers delivering {{ev:sr-cover}} of middle-overs balls. Newer spinners who qualify have already earned chances, so the comparison flatters them.
Domestic data would be needed to judge prospects before they reach the IPL.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Judge Spinners on Output, Not Age
body: Punjab Kings should judge spinners on middle-overs economy and wicket rate, not on years in the league.
Newer spinners who already match established ones on both measures are starters, whatever their experience.
